- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model underestimates upside; increase forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- If sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model underestimates downside; add 1–3% downward bias for 30d.
- Model tends to lag in early days of high event volume; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for first 3–5 days after major auction events.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment if price > 72.5 for 3+ consecutive days.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and low sentiment, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% if true outcome is below 70.5.
